title: Average distance formula
description: Essential: The student must correctly state or apply the relationship between volume, number of molecules, and average intermolecular distance (e.g., V = N d³).

title: Volume at state B
description: Important: The student must correctly determine the volume at state B from the V-T graph, recognizing the isobaric process and using the given temperatures.

title: Final distance answer
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be correctly expressed as d = ∛(2V₀/N) or an equivalent simplified form.

title: Work calculation A→B
description: Important: The student must correctly calculate the work done by the gas during the isobaric expansion from A to B, using W = -pΔV.

title: First law application
description: Essential: The student must correctly apply the first law of thermodynamics (Q = ΔU - W) for the entire process A→B→C, using the given ΔU.

title: Final heat answer
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) must be correctly expressed as Q = ΔU + pV₀.

title: Sign error in work
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the sign convention for work (W = -pΔV for work done BY gas) is mistaken, leading to an incorrect sign in the final heat expression.

title: Graph misinterpretation
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student misinterprets the V-T graph, e.g., incorrectly reading the volume at B or not recognizing the process as isobaric.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional: Award credit if the student explicitly checks or comments on the dimensional consistency of their derived expressions for distance and heat.
